name: Requirement Known
question: Core 1 asks: Do we know exactly what conforming quality means for this operation? Level 1 and Level 2 are Industry-Gold baselines. Level 3 supplies the exact customer/product/process requirement and overrides generic/local values when more specific.
boundary: Core 1 boundary: This Core defines WHAT the required quality result is. Detailed execution technique belongs in Core 2 Method Robust; prevention/control strength belongs in Core 3 Quality Built at Source; physical environment/tooling capability belongs in Cores 4 and 6; operator competence belongs in Core 7.

level_roles.L1: SWI Robustness: Industry-gold minimum for how completely and clearly the requirement must be defined in the standard work.
level_roles.L2: Station Readiness: Industry-gold minimum for how the requirement must be presented, identifiable and usable at the real station.
level_roles.L3: Customer Specific: Exact customer/product/process values, classifications, applicability, revisions, test conditions and mandatory requirements.

criteria.L1: Every quality-relevant operation states the product/process result that must be achieved or verified; an action verb alone (install, inspect, assemble, check) is not sufficient.
criteria.L2: The physical feature/result being created or verified is unambiguously identifiable at the station.
criteria.L3: The exact product/process characteristic is defined by the released customer/engineering source.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI/JES/process sheet + station image/video + engineering/customer documents
checks.primary_source: Vehicle Control Plan; Process Sheet & SWI Standard
checks.notes: Core 1 defines WHAT good is; HOW to create it belongs in Core 2.

criteria.L1: When one job affects multiple independent quality characteristics, each required result is separately identifiable in the SWI rather than buried in one generic instruction.
criteria.L2: Each characteristic can be mapped to the actual feature/location at the station.
criteria.L3: The customer/engineering requirement set identifies all applicable characteristics for the product/process.

checks.notes: Do not collapse several distinct quality outcomes into one vague instruction.

checks.requirement: Output condition stated, not only task completion

criteria.L1: The SWI distinguishes completion of the task from achievement of the required output condition.
criteria.L2: The station provides a recognizable physical/result state corresponding to the defined output condition.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering defines the actual conforming output condition.

checks.requirement: Characteristic wording is objective enough to evaluate

criteria.L1: Quality-result wording is specific enough that two trained operators should interpret the intended result the same way.
criteria.L2: The station does not introduce ambiguity about which characteristic/result is being judged.
criteria.L3: Any customer-defined terminology or characteristic naming convention is preserved.

checks.notes: Avoid words such as 'proper', 'good', 'acceptable' unless the acceptance condition is defined elsewhere.

subcategories.name: Good / Bad & Acceptance Boundary
subcategories.purpose: Define the boundary between conforming and nonconforming.

criteria.L1: For every characteristic requiring judgment, the SWI defines the acceptance boundary sufficiently to distinguish conforming from nonconforming output.
criteria.L2: The operator/inspector can compare the actual result to the acceptance boundary at the point of decision.
criteria.L3: The exact good/bad boundary comes from customer/engineering specifications, masters, defect standards, or approved criteria.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI/visual standard + station reference + customer standard

criteria.L1: Subjective terms such as appearance, flush, secure, aligned, smooth, clean, noise-free, etc. are supported by a defined reference, limit, example, or measurable boundary when they drive acceptance.
criteria.L2: The necessary reference/master/example is available under representative station conditions.
criteria.L3: Customer-specific defect definitions, zone rules, master samples, boundary samples, or other acceptance standards apply.

criteria.L1: Where inspection is required, the SWI identifies the defect/abnormality to be detected rather than only saying 'inspect' or 'check'.
criteria.L2: The defect is recognizable at the station using the provided reference/definition.
criteria.L3: Customer standards define exact defect classes, severity, size/frequency, or prohibited conditions where applicable.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI + inspection standard + customer defect criteria

criteria.L1: When a result is judged by a test, measurement, visual comparison, count, or functional check, the SWI states or references the pass/fail rule.
criteria.L2: The station display/gauge/reference permits the pass/fail decision using the same rule.
criteria.L3: Customer/process standard supplies the exact pass/fail criteria.

criteria.L1: Where normal variation can produce borderline results, the standard defines how the boundary is treated rather than leaving escalation to personal judgment.
criteria.L2: The station provides the needed reference or escalation path for borderline decisions.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering owns any exact boundary, deviation, approval, or master-sample rule.

subcategories.name: Target / Limits / Tolerance / Units
subcategories.purpose: Define measurable values, limits, tolerances and units.

criteria.L1: Every measurable quality characteristic needed by the operator is defined by a target, limit, range, or other quantitative acceptance criterion rather than 'per spec' or qualitative wording alone.
criteria.L2: The station tool/display/reference uses the same numerical requirement.
criteria.L3: The exact nominal/limits/tolerance are supplied by the released customer/engineering requirement.

criteria.L1: Every numerical requirement includes unambiguous units where units are relevant.
criteria.L2: Station indication and measurement use the same unit or an automatically controlled equivalent with no operator conversion.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering defines the authoritative unit and any allowed conversion.

checks.notes: Gold standard avoids mental conversion at point of use.

criteria.L1: One-sided requirements state whether the boundary is minimum, maximum, not-to-exceed, at-least, etc.
criteria.L2: The station makes the correct direction of acceptance obvious.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering defines the exact one-sided limit.

checks.requirement: Tolerance/band defined when nominal alone is insufficient

criteria.L1: A nominal value is not treated as a complete requirement when actual acceptance depends on an allowable band/tolerance.
criteria.L2: Station measurement or control references the correct allowable band.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering establishes the applicable tolerance/band.

checks.requirement: Count / quantity / frequency acceptance defined where product quality depends on it

criteria.L1: Where quality acceptance depends on count, number of defects, spacing, quantity, or repeated occurrences, the SWI states the applicable acceptance rule.
criteria.L2: The station supports the same count/quantity rule without forcing memory or interpretation.
criteria.L3: Customer standard supplies exact count/frequency/spacing rules.

subcategories.name: Acceptance Context / Test & Inspection Conditions
subcategories.purpose: Define the conditions under which acceptance is valid.

checks.requirement: Acceptance condition includes required test/inspection context

criteria.L1: When acceptance depends on how the result is observed or tested, the SWI states or references the necessary test/inspection conditions.
criteria.L2: The station can present the product under the required conditions when the decision is made.
criteria.L3: Customer/process standards define exact test/inspection conditions.

checks.notes: The exact station capability to achieve those conditions is assessed in later Cores; Core 1 asks whether the condition itself is known.

checks.requirement: Viewing/observation condition known when it changes acceptance

criteria.L1: Visual acceptance criteria identify any required viewing distance, orientation, surface position, zone, or equivalent observation condition when it changes good/bad interpretation.
criteria.L2: The required viewing/observation condition is identifiable and usable at the station.
criteria.L3: Customer appearance/inspection standards provide exact viewing and zone rules.

criteria.L1: When test/inspection validity depends on product condition (clean, dry, assembled state, temperature, pressure, etc.), the required precondition is stated or referenced.
criteria.L2: The station can identify whether the product is in the required precondition before judgment.
criteria.L3: Customer/process standard defines the exact precondition.

criteria.L1: Where acceptance changes by process stage or product state, the SWI identifies the correct stage/state at which the requirement applies.
criteria.L2: The station/product state is identifiable at the point the requirement is used.
criteria.L3: Customer/process standard defines the exact test stage/state.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI + process state evidence + customer/process standard

criteria.L1: If acceptance relies on a master, limit sample, gauge setting, inspection standard, checklist, or approved reference, the SWI identifies the applicable reference.
criteria.L2: The correct reference is available and clearly associated with the station/product.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering identifies the exact controlled reference and revision.

subcategories.name: Feature / Location / Zone Applicability
subcategories.purpose: Define exactly where/which feature the requirement applies to.

criteria.L1: The SWI identifies the exact feature, side, position, hole, surface, zone, connector, joint, datum, component location, etc. to which the requirement applies whenever confusion is possible.
criteria.L2: The physical location can be recognized at the station without interpretation.
criteria.L3: Customer drawing/specification defines the authoritative feature/location.

criteria.L1: When the same type of operation occurs at several locations with different requirements, each location is separately identified.
criteria.L2: The station/product presentation makes the locations distinguishable.
criteria.L3: Customer engineering defines any location-specific values or acceptance criteria.

criteria.L1: Where acceptance depends on zone/class, the SWI identifies the applicable zone/class rather than using one generic requirement.
criteria.L2: The operator/inspector can determine which zone/class is being evaluated.
criteria.L3: Customer appearance/engineering standard defines exact zone/class boundaries.

checks.requirement: Graphic or visual localization used where text is insufficient

criteria.L1: A graphic/photo/diagram is used when text alone could reasonably lead to feature/location confusion.
criteria.L2: The graphic corresponds to the actual station/product orientation.
criteria.L3: Customer/product-specific graphics or engineering views are used where necessary.

checks.requirement: Start/stop boundary of responsibility defined where quality ownership spans work zones

criteria.L1: Where operator/inspector responsibility depends on a defined work zone or start/stop boundary, the standard identifies that boundary.
criteria.L2: The boundary is visible/recognizable at the station.
criteria.L3: Customer/plant-specific boundary rules are applied where required.

subcategories.name: Product / Variant / Applicability
subcategories.purpose: Define which product/variant/build condition the requirement applies to.

criteria.L1: Each requirement identifies the car line, model, option, variant, part family, or build condition to which it applies whenever more than one can reach the station.
criteria.L2: The current build/variant is identifiable before the quality-critical decision.
criteria.L3: Customer BOM/configuration/model-year/engineering release defines exact applicability.

criteria.L1: Different variants with different requirements are not represented by one generic value/instruction.
criteria.L2: The station presents the correct active requirement for the current variant.
criteria.L3: Customer-specific values/criteria are mapped to the exact variant/configuration.

criteria.L1: The SWI structure prevents a requirement for one model/model year from being mistaken for another when products are built concurrently.
criteria.L2: The station information changes or clearly indicates which requirement applies to the current unit.
criteria.L3: Customer/model-year VCP or equivalent defines differences in characteristics/specifications.

criteria.L1: Temporary or special-build requirements are clearly distinguished from nominal production requirements.
criteria.L2: Pilot/change parts and related requirements are visibly identifiable at the station.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering change documentation defines exact temporary applicability and effective point.

criteria.L1: The operator does not need to combine multiple pieces of information mentally to determine which requirement applies.
criteria.L2: The station provides a direct link between build information and the applicable requirement/part.
criteria.L3: Customer data/configuration is translated into an unambiguous station trigger.

subcategories.name: Criticality / Classification / Regulatory Significance
subcategories.purpose: Define criticality, special status and mandatory significance.

criteria.L1: The SWI visibly identifies characteristics requiring elevated quality attention because of safety, regulatory, functional, customer, or other defined criticality.
criteria.L2: The station presentation does not hide or contradict the critical designation.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering/PFMEA/Control Plan defines the authoritative critical/special classification.

criteria.L1: The SWI uses the approved classification symbol/name rather than inventing an independent local classification.
criteria.L2: Station visuals/displays use the same classification convention.
criteria.L3: Customer/regional engineering standard defines the exact classification system.

criteria.L1: Where a characteristic becomes difficult or impossible to verify later, the SWI identifies it as a quality-critical result requiring attention at this stage.
criteria.L2: The station clearly identifies the feature before it becomes inaccessible.
criteria.L3: Customer risk assessment/PFMEA defines pass-through or hidden-feature significance.

checks.requirement: Mandatory/regulatory requirement distinguishable from discretionary controls

criteria.L1: The SWI clearly identifies mandatory requirements so they are not treated as optional/local checks.
criteria.L2: The station does not present mandatory and discretionary requirements ambiguously.
criteria.L3: Customer/regulatory documentation defines mandatory status.

subcategories.name: Source / Authority / Revision / Effective Point
subcategories.purpose: Define authoritative source, revision and effective point.

criteria.L1: Every technical quality requirement in the SWI is traceable to an approved upstream source or controlled standard.
criteria.L2: Station copies/displays/settings can be linked to the same approved requirement source.
criteria.L3: Drawing, engineering specification, process sheet, Control Plan, VCP, customer standard, etc. is the authoritative source.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI metadata/reference + station docs + source document

criteria.L1: The SWI identifies its current controlled revision/version and does not rely on uncontrolled local copies.
criteria.L2: Only the current approved requirement/reference is available at the station.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering revision status defines the authoritative current requirement.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI revision + station copy + engineering release

criteria.L1: When a requirement changes, the standard identifies when the new requirement becomes effective for production.
criteria.L2: The station can distinguish units/parts before and after the change point.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering change notice, breakpoint, model year, VIN/build event, or equivalent defines the exact effective point.

checks.evidence_inputs: Change document + station build identification + SWI

criteria.L1: Superseded values, images, samples, or instructions are removed or clearly invalidated so they cannot be used accidentally.
criteria.L2: Obsolete station references are not available as competing instructions.
criteria.L3: Customer document control defines supersession and validity.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI/document control + station audit + source revision

criteria.L1: A known deviation from the released requirement is not silently embedded in the SWI; it is identified as an approved deviation with defined scope/effective period.
criteria.L2: The station clearly identifies the approved non-nominal condition and does not treat it as normal standard.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering/quality authorization defines the exact deviation and limits.

checks.evidence_inputs: Deviation approval + temporary instruction + station visual

subcategories.name: Point-of-Use Clarity / Visual Communication
subcategories.purpose: Make the requirement usable at the point of work without interpretation.

criteria.L1: The SWI or referenced requirement is readily accessible without special access or searching during the work cycle.
criteria.L2: The information is available at the station at the moment the operator needs it.
criteria.L3: Customer-specific controlled references are available when required.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI location + station video/image + reference access

checks.requirement: Requirement visible/readable from working position when needed

criteria.L1: Critical quality information is formatted so the intended user can read and interpret it quickly.
criteria.L2: The information is visible from the actual work/inspection position when needed; it is not hidden, remote, or blocked.
criteria.L3: Customer/plant-specific display requirements are incorporated where applicable.

checks.requirement: One source of truth at point of use

criteria.L1: The operator is not required to reconcile several uncontrolled documents, boards, labels, or values to know the requirement.
criteria.L2: The station presents a single authoritative requirement or a clearly controlled hierarchy.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering source hierarchy resolves which document/value governs.

checks.requirement: No mental conversion or interpretation required

criteria.L1: The SWI avoids requiring the operator to calculate, convert, combine, decode, or infer the requirement during the cycle unless the calculation is itself standardized and error-proofed.
criteria.L2: Station information is presented directly in the form needed for the decision.
criteria.L3: Customer data is translated into the correct direct station requirement.

criteria.L1: When a requirement is easier or safer to understand visually, the SWI uses graphics/photos/symbols to make the characteristic and acceptance point unmistakable.
criteria.L2: The station visual matches the real product orientation/feature.
criteria.L3: Customer/product-specific imagery or symbols are used where necessary.

subcategories.name: Requirement Completeness / Flow-Down
subcategories.purpose: Ensure all required quality information flows into the station standard.

criteria.L1: The SWI contains or directly references every quality-result requirement the operator must know to perform the job correctly; tribal knowledge is not an acceptable source.
criteria.L2: No additional quality requirement is necessary at the station that is absent from the controlled standard.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering/PFMEA/Control Plan sources are used to expose omitted requirements.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI + station evidence + upstream quality documents
checks.supporting_source: Vehicle Control Plan; CX-F09 Control Plan

checks.requirement: Upstream engineering requirements flowed to station standard

criteria.L1: Relevant requirements from released product/process engineering documentation are carried into the station SWI.
criteria.L2: The station uses those same flowed-down requirements.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering source defines the complete requirement set.

criteria.L1: If the risk/control system identifies a characteristic as requiring operator awareness at this station, the SWI reflects that requirement.
criteria.L2: The station information aligns to the same characteristic.
criteria.L3: Customer PFMEA/Control Plan/QA Matrix determines the exact characteristic and criticality.

checks.notes: The control method itself is judged under later Cores.

checks.requirement: Known customer/field defects update requirement definition where necessary

criteria.L1: When a defect reveals that the existing definition of good was incomplete or ambiguous, the SWI is updated to include the clarified requirement.
criteria.L2: The station reference is updated consistently.
criteria.L3: Customer/warranty/audit feedback and approved engineering disposition define the added/clarified requirement.

checks.evidence_inputs: Customer defect history + revised SWI + station
checks.primary_source: CX-F01 Customer Obeya / CX-F02 Short Loop

checks.requirement: Supplier/material quality requirements visible where they affect station acceptance

criteria.L1: Where material identity/condition is part of the station's required result, the SWI states the applicable requirement rather than assuming correct material.
criteria.L2: Labels/packaging/part identification needed to recognize the requirement are available and legible.
criteria.L3: Customer/supplier/engineering standards define exact material/identification requirements.

criteria.L1: The same characteristic is not assigned multiple conflicting values, criteria, images, or statements within the controlled work instruction.
criteria.L2: Station displays, labels, tool references, masters, and SWI do not contradict one another.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering source resolves the authoritative requirement.

criteria.L1: The SWI value/criterion agrees with the approved upstream process sheet/control documentation unless an approved deviation exists.
criteria.L2: Station information/settings agree with the same requirement.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering documents are the final authority when conflict exists.

checks.evidence_inputs: SWI + process sheet + control plan + station + engineering

checks.requirement: Conflict is surfaced, not averaged or guessed

criteria.L1: If sources disagree, the SWI is not treated as robust merely because it is internally clear; the discrepancy is flagged for resolution.
criteria.L2: The station does not continue using an unresolved ambiguous requirement as if it were approved.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering authority determines the correct requirement.

checks.notes: This is a core SWP logic rule.

criteria.L1: Temporary, alternate, pilot, or exception requirements identify scope, duration/effective point, and what nominal requirement they supersede.
criteria.L2: The station visibly distinguishes non-nominal conditions from normal standard.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering/quality approval defines exact exception boundaries.

checks.supporting_source: CX-F13 Quality Change Management; CX-F11 Bypass Management

criteria.L1: Where product/component traceability is mandatory or quality-required, the SWI identifies that traceability is required for the operation/product.
criteria.L2: The station identifies which component/unit requires traceability before release.
criteria.L3: Customer/regulatory/engineering standard defines the exact component/market/model applicability.

criteria.L1: The SWI identifies the required data capture/identification outcome sufficiently for the operator to know what constitutes a complete traceability result.
criteria.L2: The station displays/captures the required identifiers in a recognizable way.
criteria.L3: Customer/engineering standard defines exact required fields, format, label/data-matrix content, VIN association, etc.

checks.notes: Exact barcode structure is Customer Specific, not universal L1/L2.

criteria.L1: The SWI distinguishes a valid traceability result from missing, unreadable, duplicate, damaged, or otherwise nonconforming identification when relevant.
criteria.L2: The station provides a clear status/result that enables the decision.
criteria.L3: Customer traceability standard defines exact nonconformance and recovery requirements.

criteria.L1: Where reprocessing or component replacement changes the traceability requirement, the SWI identifies the need to re-establish the required traceability condition.
criteria.L2: The station/rework process can recognize that traceability must be repeated or updated.
criteria.L3: Customer traceability standard defines exact re-scan/reassociation requirements.

checks.evidence_inputs: Rework SWI + station system + traceability standard
